In addition, the number of bus stations and subway stations has a restraining effect on the use of shared bicycles. Finally, the number of epidemics will increase the usage of customers and subscribers to a certain extent, with subscribers increasing by 0.25% and customer usage increasing by 2.92 %. The research results can timely analyze the usage of bicycles shared by different users among tourists during the pandemic, and can help transportation agencies adjust services in different regions to better control the spread of the virus.

articleTitle: Roadmap to safe and controllable international logistics supply chain system
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to meet the challenges of “localization”,”regionalization” and “diversification” of supply chain in developed countries and enhance China's long-term competitiveness in the global supply chain, it is necessary to take the “The Belt and Road” area as a breakthrough and plan the roadmap of China's international logistics supply chain system systematically. This paper proposes the specific roadmap: first, the basic chassis of “channel + hub + industry” of diversified channels, multi-level hubs and multi type industries are built; second, the major supports of “enterprise + platform + mechanism” of first-class enterprises, service platforms and a set of mechanisms are improved; third, tasks of “green + Finance + intelligence” of green concept, financial security and intelligent technology are upgraded.

articleTitle: Road-Railway Transport Route Optimization Considering Market Changes and Time Costs
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The customer demands for logistics service quality have seen great increase and the new development dynamic with the domestic economy and international engagement reinforcing each other has already been formed. Against such a background, it is of crucial significance to figure out how to arrange transport routes reasonably and reduce transport costs for highway-railway intermodal transport. In this study, the routes of highway-railway intermodal transport were chosen as the optimization object. A road-railway transport route optimization model targeting at the minimum total cost was constructed based on the influences of market changes on customer demands, time cost of transport and reloading cost at nodes. Moreover, a double-layer array chromosome genetic algorithm was designed to solve the model. Subsequently, a field simulation was carried out in the surrounding areas of the intersection between the Jiaozuo-Liuzhou Line and the Lanzhou-Lianyungang Line. Besides, specific suggestions for scheme and road maps were proposed in this study for intermodal transport enterprises. The scheme offered herein reduced the total cost by 36.04<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> compared with the current scheme of project, thus fully demonstrating the performance of the model proposed in the study. Finally, comparison and analysis were conducted between the double-layer array chromosome genetic algorithm and the traditional genetic algorithm, and then it has been found out that the total cost of the former was less than that of the latter by 10.56%, which verifies the performance of the algorithm proposed in this study.

articleTitle: Waterway Transportation Accidents in Ghana: A Case Study on the Volta River
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Inland waterway transportation is known to be the safest and most economical means of transportation globally. Nevertheless, the number of ferry and wooden boat accidents and associated casualties recorded annually on the Volta River have demeaned the safety and attractiveness of this mode of transportation in Ghana; as an average of 100 passengers die every year. In relation to this problem, the study is conducted based on accident data statistics and causation analysis. Open-ended structured verbal questions and researchers' observation were used to collect data on the causes of accidents and their psychological/social impact on the localities, and the necessary recommendations on how to prevent accidents as well as minimize casualties to ensure the safety of passengers and cargoes were provided. Among the many causes of accidents on the river, the most predominant ones were emerged or submerged stumps located in the navigational channel, overloading of cargoes, unprofessional boat operators, and lack of periodic boats maintenance. In this regard, the study suggested that there should be the removal of the submerged stumps, establishment of institution to coordinate inland water transportation, regular training programs for boat operators and owners, ensuring boats are equipped with life-saving equipment on board, and enforcement of punitive measures for non-compliant boat operators. Moreover, the communities along the Volta River should be included in the safety training and education as well as assist in monitoring and reporting unsafe practices to law enforcement agencies. The government should also assist with financing of safety projects and provision of requisite equipment to trainers and agencies to ensure effective discharge of their responsibilities on the river. These are aimed towards preventing accidents on the Volta River.

articleTitle: Determine Lane Function of Variable Approach Lane at the Signalized Intersection Based on Real-time Traffic Status
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: How to determine the lane function of Variable Approach Lane (VAL) is critical for satisfying the turning traffic demand and decreasing vehicle delay. Though a lot of scholars have studied this topic, most of them ignore the cycle-by-cycle traffic demand fluctuation at a signalized intersection. This paper proposes a dynamic offline lane assignment scheme to determine the lane function of VAL based on real-time traffic status identification. Firstly, the Fuzzy C- Means Algorithm is utilized to identify the traffic status based on three indicators: volume, occupancy, and speed in a cycle. Then, a rapid traffic status identification system focusing on through and left-turn traffic is built. A dynamic lane assignment model is established to determine the lane function of VAL in a real-time manner. An example is introduced to better illustrate how the method works. The result shows that the number of vehicles released increases by 9.8% while the delay per vehicle is reduced by 9.2%. In addition, the performance of dynamic lane, fixed left-turn lane, and fixed through lane under different traffic volumes is compared and results show dynamic lane has the best performance. Finally, this paper compares the proposed dynamic lane optimization method with two other optimization methods. Results reveal that the proposed method works better.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional Simulation of Emergency Evacuation of Large Cruise Ship Based on Path Network with Width
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Aiming at the improvement of emergency evacuation efficiency of cruise ship, three-dimensional emergency evacuation simulations were studied. As to the evacuation model construction, firstly, the road network model with width was proposed, based on which the algorithm of dense crowd passing in road sections with width, as well as the algorithm of evacuation path searching considering distance and traffic flow were proposed. Besides, an improved model of individual collision avoidance was proposed. As to the simulation system, taking a large cruise ship as an example, based on the three-dimensional ship model, the road sections model with width were built, and the spatial nodes such as rooms, restaurants and cinemas were connected to form a path network with width. then the path network of each floor was connected with the evacuation exit to form an evacuation topology network of the whole ship. With the support of the proposed path finding algorithm and the improved individual collision avoidance model, the simulation of emergency evacuation processes were realized and the cruise ship emergency evacuation three-dimensional simulation system was developed. Based on the three-dimensional simulation system, the paper focuses on the simulation of different escape exit layout and different evacuation strategies. By comparing and analyzing the simulation results, the key factors affecting the efficiency and safety of emergency evacuation of cruise ships are accurately identified, which can provide auxiliary support for the design of space layout and evacuation facilities of cruise ships and the optimization of emergency evacuation plan.

articleTitle: A Fast Stable Lane Change Path Planning Method Based On Hybrid Intelligent Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: To improve the solving speed and success rate of the lane change path planning problem for autonomous vehicles, a fast and stable planning method (FSDETS) is proposed in this paper. This lane change path planning scheme is formulated as an optimal control problem according to the three-segment lane change model. Then the B-spline curve is applied to smooth the path. The core contribution is that a method based on hybrid intelligent algorithms is proposed to solve the optimal control problem fast and stably. First, an extended differential evolution is proposed to quickly provide a tough initial guess for the subsequent search. Then two criteria are set to judge whether the tabu search can start. After satisfying them, tabu search seeks a better solution based on the initial guess. Finally, a 1000 cycles simulation experiment is run to verify its stability and real-time performance. Simulation results show that the average time consumption is 0.7417ms, the success rate is 99.97% and the average maximum curvature is 0.13947m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Besides, it is also compared with other intelligent optimization algorithms as well as the optimization solver MIDACO. The result shows that our method surpasses other algorithms in comprehensive performances.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization of Community Bus and Flexible Feeder Bus Connection System
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Along with the development of public transportation network in china, the connection between rail transit and conventional buses still needs further improvement. Designing an efficient feeder-bus network is essential for improving metro hubs’ distribution capacity. This paper divides the operation of the flexible feeder bus system into two stages. The first stage is to cluster travel demands with similar spatiotemporal characteristics, and then construct RLMP, SPS problems by using the column generation algorithm, which can reduce system travel cost and complete vehicle route planning at the same time. In the second stage, the mixed decision optimization of vehicle service attributes is carried out based on the reverse auction algorithm, which can minimize its impact on community bus and meet the demands of flexible bus operation. Finally, based on the bus operation data of three community bus routes near a subway station in Chengdu, it's verified that this model has good effects both on operational efficiency and benefits.

articleTitle: Integrity Monitoring of GNSS-based Vehicle Positioning based on Cooperative Weighting Strategy
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the rapid development of Cooperative Intelligent Transportation System (C-ITS) and the vehicle-infrastructure cooperation technology, there have been new requirements for the integrity monitoring of urban vehicle positioning based on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). The existing weight evaluation solutions based on certain satellite observation information have to be enhanced for advanced GNSS-enabled applications. Under the cooperative vehicle-infrastructure scheme, this paper investigates the novel GNSS weighting method by combining the GNSS observation information from the subject vehicle and its neighborhoods in a local area. The Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN) is utilized to build prediction models to describe the relationship between the satellite observation information and pseudo-range residual. With the off-line models, weight of GNSS measurements can be real-timely evaluated by integrating the information of all connected vehicles within a specific region area, which makes good use of the cooperation by wireless communication. Experiments were carried out to compare the proposed cooperative weighting strategy and other related methods. The results demonstrate the capability and potentials of this proposal in integrity monitoring by over-bounding the horizontal position error with the horizontal protection level, which is significant in many safety-related GNSS applications in novel transportation systems.

articleTitle: Difference analysis of intelligent energy efficiency management system of ships using different power
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Affected by policies and regulations such as energy saving, emission reduction and cost reduction and efficiency enhancement, the shipping industry has a high demand for intelligent energy efficiency management systems for ships. First, the main functional modules of the ship's intelligent energy efficiency management system are analyzed; then, with regard to three types of ships i.e. diesel power, hybrid power, and battery power, the structure of different power systems and their power transmission paths are studied, in the meantime, the difference analyses of the ship's intelligent energy efficiency management system was carried out from the four aspects of energy efficiency monitoring, evaluation, optimization and hardware architecture. Finally, the differences of the energy efficiency management system were summarized, and its generalization and modular development were prospected. This research has guiding significance for the development of intelligent energy efficiency management systems for different powered ships.

articleTitle: An Experimental Investigation of Novice and Experienced Drivers' Car Following Task Performance on Snowy Road
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Driving on snowy road is different from dry road due to reduced friction. Novice drivers may have more problems driving on snowy road due to the lack of experience, e.g., driving too fast, frequently baking, turning the steering wheel at will, braking and avoiding at the same time. It is an important issue for legislation, automotive tire design and driving safety training. This study compared the effect of snowy road versus dry road on driving performance in a driving simulator by asking participants to perform a car-following task. Results showed that both inexperienced and snowy driving impaired driving performance by causing more variation in lane position. The accelerating response time of the drivers, speed and headway distance was increased on snowy road. These results provided suggestions for snowy-road specific countermeasures and driving safety training.

articleTitle: A Novel Artificial Potential Field Based Ship Path Planning Algorithm Using Model Predictive Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: There exist some limitations and defects when the conventional artificial potential field (APF) based methods are utilized for ship path planning, especially in complex navigation scenarios. In consideration of the path planning requirements for emerging autonomous or smart ships, a novel path planning algorithm that combined the improved artificial potential field method with model predictive control is proposed. A novel potential field function is proposed to achieve collision avoidance and target point arrival in complex waters. Then, ship maneuverability based on the Nomoto model is considered to generate the trackable path. Moreover, the path planning problem is converted to a nonlinear optimization problem, and maneuverability models, position update methods, etc., are considered in the constraints. Finally, the path planning problem is solved using model predictive strategy and online optimization algorithm. We verify the effectiveness of the MPC with different prediction steps in a multi-obstacle scenario. The simulation results show that compared to traditional APF and particle swarm optimization (PSO)-based APF, the proposed algorithm can generate a safer and more feasible path in complex scenarios and meet the real-time requirements.

articleTitle: Global food supply chain resilience assessment: A case in the United Kingdom
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As a result of Coronavirus disease (Covid-19), container trade volumes and container port throughputs in the world have both declined over the first half of 2020. Covid - 19 causes unprecedented disruptions to the countries where food supplies heavily rely on shipping, such as the United Kingdom (UK). It is vital to assess the associated food shipping systems to ensure national food supply resilience. This paper aims to assess the national food supply chain (FSC) resilience for the UK by considering food import dependency and shipping transport connectivity. A new national food connectivity index (NFCI) framework is formulated, and supporting data is collected from the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD), Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), and the United Nations Commodity Trade (UN Comtrade). NFCI of the UK is calculated and compared with other countries. The formulation and analysis contribute to a newly proposed formal method to assess a nation's FSC resilience and observe and address the shortcomings of its food supply system for food security.

articleTitle: Study on Influence Factors of Carbon Emission in Hubei's Logistics Industry Based on LMDI Method
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: China's total carbon emissions have surpassed those of the United States and the European Union, and becomes the largest carbon emitter in the world. As the vanguard of the national economy, the logistics and transportation industry is closely related to energy consumption and carbon emission. Based on this, this paper takes the logistics industry as the research subject,and takes the energy consumption of the logistics transportation industry in Hubei Province as the basic data, Using the LMDI decomposition method, first this paper analyzes the present situation and the trend change of the carbon emission of the logistics transportation industry in Hubei Province, then the paper analyzes the driving factors that affect the change of carbon emission intensity of logistics industry in Hubei Province, and finally puts forward some suggestions and measures on the low-carbon path of logistics industry in Hubei Province, which can provide effective support for the development of low-carbon industry in Hubei Province

articleTitle: Numerical simulation analysis of the stability of lifeboats during release under high sea conditions
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: As the main water rescue vehicle, lifeboats are an important guarantee for the safety of crew and passengers. During the release of the survival crafts affected by extreme conditions, such as mother ship shaking and strong winds, the survival crafts will move violently in multiple degrees of freedom directions, which may cause collision or the failure of the lifeboat launching devices. As a result, it will lead to the rescue efficiency reduction and crew casualties. In this paper, the 3D model of lifeboat system was established by SolidWorks firstly. Based on equation of the Lagrange, the dynamic simulation software ADAMS/View was used to model and analyze the relationship between the hull roll, pitch, wind load and the release length of the davit cable and the response of the lifeboat, that is, the amplitude and frequency of its swing. The simulation results show that the ship's rolling and pitching exert the most significant effect on the lifeboat's release process, and the wind load generally does not cause the lifeboat's dangerous swing. Lifeboat swings weaker and weaker as it gets closer to the sea. Therefore, the design of the controller to actively control the expansion of the boom and the release speed of the boat winch is helpful to realize collision avoidance and shimmy reduction and improve the safety of the lifeboat in the release process. The research results can provide theoretical basis and guidance for the design and operation of the release mechanism of various types of lifeboats.

articleTitle: Design and Test of an Experimental Platform for Unmanned Surface Vessel
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper establishes an unmanned surface vessel (USV) experimental platform for different mission requirements and research experiments. The experimental platform consists of software and hardware parts. The hardware part includes its electronic control system, communication system and propulsion system. The software part includes a software system based on the Robot Operating System (ROS) framework and a simulation platform based on Gazebo. This paper proposed a robust type2-fuzzy logic (T2FLS) controller to tackle system uncertainties and external disturbances, and the simulation results show the feasibility and effectiveness of this algorithm. The designed control algorithm is verified using a Gazebo implementation in the frame of ROS. This paper developed a Gazebo simulation platform which can debug the control algorithm, simulate the marine environment, and establish an ocean current interference model. Since the input and output interfaces in the simulation environment are consistent with the existing USV system, the actual USV experiment can be carried out directly after the simulation with no code conversion and other operations, thus simplifying the work and speeding up the experiment progress.

articleTitle: Optimization of China-Europe Refrigerated Container Train Operation Plan Based on Hub-and-Spoke Network
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: According to the demand of multi-origin and multi-category refrigerated cargo transportation, this paper studies the optimization problem of China-Europe refrigerated container train operation plan based on hub-and-spoke service network. In this paper, we analyse transportation cost, refrigeration cost, time value cost and assembly center loading and unloading cost, according to the operation process of direct trains, connecting trains and transfer trains. This paper puts forward an optimization model, which minimizes the total cost of service network, considering the opportunity constraints of uncertain demand. Based on this model, genetic algorithm is designed to solve the problem to obtain the best assembly center, the train plan and the container flow allocation plan. The validity and maneuverability of the model and algorithm are verified by a numerical example. The results show that the train plan considering the uncertain demand has higher transport capacity and lower average cost, which provides scientific decision support for the train plan design of China-Europe refrigerated container train.

Author Keywords: train plan of China-Europe Railway Express

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation of Multimodal Transport Node Service Levels
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The multimodal transport node, as the key hub of a comprehensive transport network, realizes the efficient transfer and organization of goods between various transport modes. The service level improvement of multimodal transport nodes is of great significance to promote the development of multimodal transport. However, limited researches have been conducted to systematically evaluate the service level of multimodal transport node (SLMTN). To fill in this gap, this paper establishes an evaluation index system of the SLMTN by systematically analyzing the components of multimodal transport nodes. An evaluation model based on the hierarchical-grey correlation analysis method is used and verified by a case study. The result shows the model can provide references for the evaluation of SLMTN, facilitate the development of multimodal transport.

articleTitle: Lithium-ion Battery Risk Assessment for New Energy Vehicles Based on Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Accurate alarms for Lithium-ion battery faults are essential to ensure the safety of New Energy Vehicles(NEVs). Related research shows that the change characteristics of the battery are important parameters reflecting the fault of NEVs. In this study, the ferrous lithium phosphate batteries data of 30 NEVs for 9 months in the National Monitoring and Management Center for New Energy Vehicles (NMMC-NEV) was analyzed. In addition to the measurement defined in GB/T 32960–2016, new indicators that can reflect the characteristics of battery changes are also analyzed, which are: Euro per volt (Ω/V), the maximum cell voltage difference, and the maximum cell temperature difference. Binary Logistic regression analysis was used to extract characteristic indicators related to three fault alarms: UnderVoltage_Alarm, OverVoltage_Alarm, and Insulation_Alarm, and the definition of the fault level is defined according to GB/T 32960-2016: satisfied, acceptable, tolerable, and unacceptable. A novel quantitative evaluation method for battery risk assessment was proposed by using Bayesian networks. Then, the robustness and reliability of the model was verified based on historical operating data, when some kind of fault alarm occurs (the probability of the fault alarm is 100%), the risk assessment result is consistent with the risk status interval divided according to the fault level. Verification results show that this study can assess potential fault risk timely and accurately.

articleTitle: Use of a system-theoretic model for safety analysis of remotely-controlled system of inland ships
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: During the last decade, the remotely-controlled ships had developed rapidly because of the potential advantages of improving safety, reducing emissions, and reducing manning. Due to the safety of remotely-controlled system is the important foundation in the research for remotely-controlled ships, this paper proposed a remotely-controlled system for different levels of autonomy and with or without crew on board. And the safety of the system is analyzed by using the system-theoretic process analysis (STPA) approach. The analysis results indicate that: (1) Among the 13 types of system-level hazards, virtual captain failure, remotely-controlled station failure and communication error have the largest number of unsafe control actions, and the number of corresponding safety strategies is also the largest, which accounts for more than 10%; (2) The potential risk failures of the remotely-controlled system of inland ships mainly include five categories: hardware equipment failure, system software failure, communication factor, human error and environmental factor; (3) When the level of autonomy is improved, the risk of collision and wave damage caused by communication error will be reduced or eliminated. And the number of effective safety strategies will also increase, while the number of safety strategies will decrease; (4) When there are crews on board, the number of most effective safety strategies will increase by 10, and the total number of safety strategies will increase by 20. The results are helpful to improve the safety of the remotely-controlled system of inland ships in the preliminary design stage, by designing the safety strategies for different autonomy levels and with or without crew on board.

articleTitle: Improved Time-to-collision Considering Vehicle Speed Adaptation based on Trajectory Data
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: For vehicle-vehicle conflicts, existing safety surrogate analyses are mainly based on the assumption of constant velocity. However, this assumption ignores the maneuver adaptations in the process of vehicle-vehicle interaction. In order to assess the risk during vehicle-vehicle interaction in a more accurate way, this paper proposes an improved TTC measure. The new TTC measure takes into account the impact of vehicle interactions by considering speed adaptations by the leading and following vehicle. The speed distribution was extracted from the Shanghai Naturalistic Driving Study data to calibrate the new TTC measure. A case study is then conducted to test the new safety measure. The result shows that the improved TTC presents different results from the traditional TTC measure illustrating the new measure potentially describe the crash risk in car-following conditions in a more detailed and precise way. The study will provide new ideas and methods in a more accurate and robust way for traffic conflict analysis.

articleTitle: An Improved Social Force Model Considering View Angle for Microscopic Pedestrian Simulation
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper proposes an Improved Social Force Model (ISFM) considering the pedestrian and obstacle neighborhoods to simulate the micro-behavior of pedestrians in different scenes. Specially, the proposed model also considers different view angle sensitivities of one pedestrian to other obstacles and pedestrians. A simulation algorithm is proposed for the ISFM, which reduces the algorithm's complexity from polynomial complexity to linear complexity of pedestrian amount. Finally, a complex scene of metro passengers alighting and boarding the train is implemented to demonstrate the performance and efficiency of the ISFM. The result shows that the proposed algorithm improves the simulation efficiency while maintaining the accuracy of the original model.

articleTitle: Travel pattern variation effects on utility factor after COVID-19: an empirical case
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Carbon emission is largely reduced during the COVID-19 due to the lockdown. However, the accurate impact in the personal transport sector after the epidemic is still not clear. To accurately measure the travel pattern variation effects on utility factor of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV s) due to COVID-19, travel pattern, charging pattern, and utility factors (UF) are compared in a typical city based on actual travel data before and after the pandemic. The result shows that the number of trips and the daily vehicle kilometers travelled decreased significantly during the pandemic while the average daily travel mileage increased quickly after the pandemic and is only 9% lower than that before the pandemic. Some consumers even travel longer with personal vehicles to avoid possible health risks from public transportation. The electricity utility factor after the pandemic is 0.022 larger compared to that before the pandemic due to the variation of travel patterns, a 60-km-range PHEV has a pre-pandemic standard UF of 0.745 and a post-pandemic standard UF of 0.767. Besides, the actual UF is 15% smaller compared to the standard UF due to the actual charging frequency in reality.

articleTitle: Repair Strategies of an Urban Rail Transit Network Based on Optimal Resilience
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Determining optimal repair sequences of failed stations has great significance to improve its operations under disturbances. Considering the URT stations' failure severities, a repair strategy which is called the model repair strategy is proposed to determine the repair sequences of failed stations under disturbances. The model repair strategy aims at minimizing a URT network's performance loss and maximizing repair efficiency, and it is constrained by the amount of repair resource and repair capacity. The model repair strategy is solved by the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm. Finally, the repair strategies for the Chengdu subway network under random and deliberate attacks are calculated by the model and staci repair strategies. The results indicate that deliberate attacks are more harmful to the Chengdu subway network than random attacks. Compared with the static repair strategy, the model repair strategy has greater repair efficiency. It can effectively reduce a URT network's performance loss caused by the disturbances. The operators are encouraged to apply the model repair strategy to determine the repair sequences of failed stations.

articleTitle: Research and simulation of freight vehicle cooperative adaptive cruise formation control model
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In this paper, five vehicles were formed in formation, and millimeter-wave radar was used to collect the relative position and velocity information of the vehicles. Based on the vehicle safety distance model, a Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (CACC) model was established. Through Matlab/Simulink and TruckSim co-simulation, the feasibility of the system is initially verified. The simulation results show that: in the process of following the vehicle, the distance between the front and rear vehicles always fluctuates within the set safety range, which has good safety; the relative speed and relative distance of the last four vehicles fluctuate very little and has good stability. The control algorithm considering relative speed and relative distance can not only ensure the safety of vehicles in the process of running but also make the following accuracy between vehicles better.

articleTitle: Increasing the reliability of marine main engines-An experimental study on magnetoresistance monitoring for piston ring wear
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The reliability of ship's power systems plays an important pole in the safe navigation of ships, in which, the reliability of main engines, which is the “heart” of ships), is one of the most crucial factors. Therefore, it is of great necessity and significance to realize the monitoring failure of ship's main engines in order to ensure that they can work properly. In view of this, this research proposed a method for the online monitoring piston ring wear of marine main engines based on the magnetic sensor technology. To verify the proposed method, a piston ring wear test bed was built, and the wear test of piston ring of two main engines with different cylinder diameter was carried out accordingly. Meanwhile, the magneto resistance signals of the two piston rings in different wear conditions were collected and analyzed comparatively. The results show that, firstly, both of the wear conditions of the two piston rings have a one-to-one correspondence with the characteristic values of the magneto-resistance signal; secondly, with the increase of the wear volume, the peak value of the magneto resistance signal shows an upward trend, thus verifying the effectiveness and adaptability of this method in terms of online monitoring wear of piston ring. The proposed method has the advantages of online, fast response and convenient use. This research provides a good reference for the whole-life monitoring of piston rings of main engines and the condition-based maintenance of main engines on board ships as well.

articleTitle: Design on Freeway Automatic Incident Detection System Based on Edge Computing and AI Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Accurate, fast and real-time freeway automatic incident detection can improve the freeway intelligence level to a great extent. Based on edge computing and artificial intelligence algorithms, the framework of freeway automatic incident detection system is proposed in this study. The core structure relying on edge computing is presented initially and a series of intelligent algorithms are employed to extract, identify, track and predict the trajectory of the object vehicles. Various scenarios of incidents are detected and pre-warned. The testing results reveal that the system can provide higher accuracy for the incident detection purpose.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Layout of Separate Lock Station in Automated Container Terminal
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Lock station layout affects the efficiency of automated container terminal operations. For this reason, a lock station layout strategy must be studied to solve the problem. In this work, based on the traditional lock station layout strategy, we propose a separate lock station layout strategy in which the lock station, QC (Quay Crane) and yard are physically isolated, and the lock station no longer occupies the lane of QC operation area. The simulation results demonstrates that the separated lock station layout strategy can reduce the average waiting time of ART (Artificial Intelligence Robot of Transportation) at the lock station by 99%, and increase the lock station utilization by 22%, which has good practical application value, compared with the traditional method.

articleTitle: Research on Water Distribution in the Circular Curve Section of the Highway
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to study the influence of geometric alignment of highway circular curve section on water thickness distribution of road area, the standard orthogonal test was established with the leading research variables of the transverse slope, longitudinal slope, road width, and circular curve radius. The water distribution of the road's surface was simulated based on computational fluid dynamics. The influence of transverse slope, longitudinal slope, road width, and circular curve radius on water thickness was compared by numerical analysis. The results show that the larger the number of lanes, the larger the peak value of accumulated water thickness. Under the rainfall intensity of 3.5mm/min, the maximum water thickness of a four-lane circular curve road is 11 mm, six-lane is 16mm, eight-lane is 22mm. The water thickness on the surface of the circular curve road is positively correlated with the height and width and negatively correlated with the longitudinal slope. There is no apparent linear relationship between the radius of the circular curve and the thickness of the water. The influence degree of the water thickness on the surface of the circular curve road is road width > transverse slope > longitudinal slope > circular curve radius.

articleTitle: Simulation analysis of load characteristics of water-lubricated bearing slats based on ANSYS
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The slat structure of water-lubricated bearings is relatively complicated. The research of slats is mainly focused on improving the vibration, noise and lubrication effect of water-lubricated bearings. There are few dynamic load monitoring methods for water-lubricated bearing rubber slats. Before the load monitoring of the slats, if the internal load distribution of the slats can be obtained, it can provide guidance for the installation of embedded strain sensors. The finite element method is used, combined with the Hertz contact theory and the RNG k-s turbulence model, and the numerical simulation of the water-lubricated bearing in the contact state and the hydrodynamic lubrication state is carried out. The bottom slat is taken as the research object, and the influence of factors such as speed and external load on the load characteristics of slat is studied. The results show that: In the contact state, the load of the slat is mainly concentrated in the contact area, and is close to the end face and the water tank. The axial load is distributed in an M shape, and the circumferential load distribution is large at both ends and small in the middle. As the journal load increases, the slat load increases, and the load distribution becomes more uneven, especially near the two ends. Under the condition of hydrodynamic lubrication, as the speed increases, the high-pressure area of the water film gradually moves from the inlet to the center of the bearing. At 500 rpm, the internal load distribution of the slats is almost consistent with the water film pressure distribution, and the load is mainly concentrated near the inlet and the water tank. The research work is helpful to provide theoretical guidance for on-line monitoring of water-lubricated bearing.

articleTitle: Case studies on the impact of flap rudders on ship maneuverings
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The impact of flap rudders on ship maneuverings is studied in this paper. CFD calculations are performed on both 3D and 2D flap rudders, and a transformation formulation, which can lighten the computational burdens, is proposed to connect the relation of these results. By conducting a series of simulations on flap rudder with different configurations, a flap rudder force model is obtained by regression methods. After that, based on a semi-empirical maneuverability mathematical model, typical maneuvers of a KVLCC2 model equipped with various flap rudders are simulated, while motion parameters during these maneuvers are compared to show how flap rudders affect the maneuverability performance of ships.

articleTitle: Time-varying Regularity Exploration and Regulation Practice of Driving Fatigue
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Among the main factors affecting driving fatigue, consecutive driving time and corresponding rest time are considered to be the most direct factors. As a state variable, driving fatigue of the driver has a gradual accumulation process during the driving. It is necessary to study the time-varying regularity of the entire cycle of driver fatigue. This article provides a review of time-varying regularity of motor vehicle driving fatigue and fatigue driving management method. The research results and regulations on reasonable consecutive driving time and rest time of drivers all over the world are summarized. The limitations of the researches on driver fatigue state judging or prediction and fatigue time-varying regularity are discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization Design and Safety Assessment of Traffic Facilities in Freeway Tunnel Area
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to improve the safety level of highway long tunnel, the visual reference frame of the tunnel was reconstructed based on line-of-sight guidance technology, which proposed to use shading sheds, reflective strips and rings as improvement facilities to optimize the tunnel light environment. Twenty subjects were recruited to carry out driving simulation test, and the characterization data of longitudinal driving states such as speed, acceleration and accelerator pedal were extracted and analyzed. Finally, the technique for order preference by similarity to an ideal solution (TOPSIS) method was adopted to evaluate the improvement scheme. The statistical results show that the average speed, acceleration standard deviation, and throttle efficiency of the driver in the optimized scenario are lower than those of the conventional scenario from 300m in front of the tunnel to the exit of the tunnel, and the acceleration fluctuation range of the optimized scenario is smaller than that of the conventional scenario. The results of TOPSIS suggested that the safety, comfort, and stability of the driver's performance in the optimized scene have been improved. The findings have certain reference significance for improving the safety of the freeway tunnel area.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault Based on Wavelet Transform and PSO-SVM
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The inter-turn short circuit fault is a common fault in the drive motor which has a serious hazard to the safe operation of the motor. However, due to the high concealment of the inter-turn short circuit fault, it is difficult to find the fault in the initial stage. Therefore, how to diagnose it in the early stage becomes extremely important. This paper presents a fault diagnosis method of motor inter-turn short circuit based on wavelet transform and optimized support vector machine. First, the wavelet transform is used to decompose the motor phase current, and input the decomposed energy vector of each frequency band as the identification feature into the support vector machine classifier. At the same time, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the penalty factor and kernel parameters of the support vector machine to ensure The model has high diagnostic power.

articleTitle: China's Vessel Security System under the Background of the Revision of Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China: Connotation and Development
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Since the 21st century, piracy, armed hijacking and terrorist attacks have occurred frequently, threatening the safety of international maritime transportation and the interests of shipping enterprises. Under such circumstance, in order to satisfy the requirements of shipping development and respond to the maritime threats, the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (2021) has been revised based on the notion of rationality and feasibility. This paper analyses the Articles 12, 32 and 38 of the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (2021), which jointly constitute the legal basis of China's vessel security system. Such security system is applicable to the coastal waters under the jurisdiction of China, international ships of Chinese nationality and related maritime safety activities. We find the security system not only protects the safety of China's maritime transport activities, but also provides certain protection for the interests of shipping enterprises in various countries. At present, the provisions of the MTSL for the vessel security system are relatively general. To implement security vessel system in the future, China may refer to other countries' legislation and state practice to further apply these articles.

articleTitle: A qualitative Study on the Situation of Helicopter Rescue in Hazardous Chemicals Accident at sea
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The development driving force of emergency response industry for hazardous chemicals accident at sea mainly comes from large-scale marine accidents. The collision and sinking of “Sanchi” in 2018 is the first accident in the world shipping history in which an oil tanker carrying “condensate” was collided and caught fire. Due to the continuous volatility and flammability of condensate, rescue is relatively difficult. In addition, the oil film continued to spread on the sea, and the difficulty of control and cleaning is relatively high. All of these lead to a greater impact on human life, environment and economy, which has sounded an alarm for China's emergency response ability of hazardous chemicals accident. In this paper, based on the background of hazardous chemicals accident at sea, the basic principles of rescue helicopter participating in such rescue missions are discussed, and the relevant suggestions for the development of the industry are put forward.

articleTitle: Study on optimal location of Pilot Boarding waters in Guangzhou Port
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The characteristics of widespread port, long pilotage routes and complex navigation environment in the pilotage waters of Guangzhou port bring about the problems of long pilotage time and high pilotage risk to the pilotage operation of Guangzhou port. And the siting of pilot boarding waters is related to the safety of pilotage operation, the navigation safety of surrounding ships and the operation efficiency of the port. Based on the analysis of the characteristics and requirements of the pilot boarding waters, this paper elaborates the optimal siting scheme for the pilot boarding waters at Guangzhou Port, which establishes a multi-objective siting model for the pilot boarding waters, combines the actual situation of the pilotage operation in Guangzhou Port and the pilotage area, and uses genetic algorithm to solve the model problem. Compared with the current setting situation of pilot boarding waters at Guangzhou Port, this paper also explores whether there is a better setting and siting scheme for pilot boarding waters.

articleTitle: Updating of Complex FEM Model of Air-cushion-vehicle Flexible Skirt in Abaqus
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Based on the configuration of air cushion vehicle flexible skirt and its loaded force, a solution to update complex model of skirt was presented. Through application developments by Visual LISP in AutoCAD and by VBA in CATIA, it can automatically parse nodes with same coordinate on neighbor ear flaps of neighbor fingers and differentiate to form independent left and right ear flap, and merge finger foreface with left / right side ears to form a whole finger mesh. It can also parse skirt outer / inner attach edge to add hull bottom and side cline into mesh model. Finally, it can extract finger deformation from analysis result file (*.odb) in Abaqus and parse boundary edge of finger contacting with ground. For the updated FEM model, each whole finger from hundred could be selected easily, loaded by force, assert un-penetrate restriction between neighbor ear flaps, parse finger position touching with ground during post-process, then form basis for further analysis.

articleTitle: Crew Fatigue Risk Analysis of Three Intercontinental Flights from China during the COVID-19 Epidemic Period
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Fatigue leads to the decrease of the flight crew's alertness, which will seriously affect the flight safety. In order to avoid the risk of infection caused by the overnight stay abroad of the air crew during the Covid-19 epidemic, CAAC proposed an exemption method to release the flight time restriction of regulation by increasing the number of flight crew and setting up an independent rest area on international flights. Based on the alertness energy theory, this paper simulates the crew alertness of three international scheduled flights of China Southern Airlines, including Guangzhou - Amsterdam, Guangzhou - Los Angeles, and Guangzhou - Sydney, to compare the difference of crew alertness between “3 sets of flight crew, without overnight rest” in accordance with exemption condition, and “2 sets of flight crew, with overnight rest” in accordance with regulation condition. The simulation results show that for the Guangzhou - Amsterdam and Guangzhou - Los Angeles flights, the cockpit alertness under the exemption condition is similar to that under the regulation condition, and the fatigue risk is acceptable; for the “Guangzhou-Sydney” flight, because the return flight under the exemption condition is always in the negative range of human rhythm, the alertness is lower than that under the regulation condition.

articleTitle: Remote Control of Ships Based on Twin Vision
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In this paper, a ship remote control system based on twin vision is proposed from the perspective of ship control under three-dimensional environment. The system loads the global image data and 3D models information of Google map through Cesium system. To quickly load the 3D models information, the system adopts 5G network to receive and send the data, and continuously sends the data of the automatic identification system (AIS) installed on the ship to the remote-control terminal through 5G network. Cesium on the remote-control terminal according to the received information to carry out 3D rendering of the controlled ship and other ships, thus generating the twin vision of the controlled ship in real time. To achieve the purpose of fast remote control, the remote-control terminal sends control signals to the controlled ship through the 5G network. When the controlled ship receives the signals, it starts corresponding actions immediately. At this time, Cesium will draw the twin visual images of the controlled ship in real time according to the AIS data received by the remote-control terminal. The remote-control terminal continuously receives AIS data and sends ship control signals through 5G network, and the CESIUM system can complete the remote rapid control of the ship by drawing the twin visual images of the controlled ship in real time, which enables the remote controller to grasp the dynamic information of the ship in real time.

articleTitle: Research on the Control Method of Oil Injection Lubrication for Marine Low-speed Engine Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: This paper takes a marine low-speed engine as the research object and establishes a cylinder liner-piston ring lubrication model based on the time-varying supply characteristics of cylinder lubricating oil. By changing the oil injection position, oil film thickness, oil distribution range, etc., the cylinder oil injection control parameters are controlled and analyzed. Influence on the lubrication performance of cylinder liner-piston ring. The results show that when the cylinder oil feed rate is 1.0 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{g}/\mathbf{kW}\cdot \mathbf{h}$</tex>, the oil injection point is located 1.5 m above the bottom dead center of the piston, and the renewed oil film thickness is 10.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex>, the frictional power loss(FPL) of one stroke is the lowest.

articleTitle: Structural Noise Removal for Imaging Sonar: A Case Study for BlueView Imaging Sonar
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In underwater acoustic vision based applications, a BlueView imaging sonar is advantageous for its long signal propagation distance and strong penetrating ability. However, the sonar images are generally suffering from structural noise due to interference and reverberation, which brings a target-like pattern and severely hinders the corresponding measurement and interpretation process. Most previous work assumes identical independent Gaussian noise model, which is potentially not well-suited to structure noise. Instead, we ultimately adopt pixel-wise adapted Gaussian mixture models to represent the noise distribution for each individual pixel based on the investigation of the noise characteristic. The parameters of each model are consequently learned from real image data via an expectation-maximization algorithm. Utilizing the noise models, the structure noise is primally suppressed through probabilistic thresholding and further removed via median filtering. Experimental results on both simulated and real data validate the effectiveness and efficiency of our method.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Adaptive Cruise Control in Mixed Traffic Flow Considering Different Time Headway Policies
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Emerging connected and autonomous vehicles (CAVs) technologies are expected to be the most promising technology for improving traffic efficiency and safety. However, high-level CAVs are unavailable in near future. As a low-level application of CAVs, adaptive cruise control (ACC) is widely applicable in the academy and industry. In the long term, ACC vehicles will co-exist with human-driven vehicles on the road. There is an urgent need to have a comprehensive understanding of driving behaviors for ACC in mixed traffic flow. For the ACC algorithms, the key component is the desired time headway policy, and it will directly affect vehicle safety and traffic efficiency. Currently, two types of desired time headway policies can be distinguished for ACC: constant time headway (CTH) and variable time headway (VTH). In this paper, the performance comparison of ACC in mixed traffic flow with different desired time headway policies is conducted. First, the string stability conditions of the mixed traffic flow with different desired time headway policies for ACC are analytically derived. Then, simulation experiments of mixed traffic flow with different penetration rates of ACC vehicles are conducted considering an on-ramp bottleneck. The safety and efficiency performance of the mixed traffic flow with different desired time headway policies of ACC vehicles are calculated. Results show that the VTH policy has better performance for improving safety and efficiency compared with the CTH policy.

articleTitle: Emergency Evacuation of Passengers With Collective Behaviors for the Ferry Station
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: It has been accepted that reliability analysis is a fundamental tool for evaluating the ferry station security of passenger emergency service. The ferry passengers emergency effective management measures, by improving the security significance of the ferry station. In this paper, the research emergency strategies for the ferry passengers emergency is organized in a LIFO (Last In First Out) strategy combining the collective behaviors. Secondly, the cellular automaton model to describe the dynamic characteristics of the ferry passengers during the emergency evacuation of ferry station. Numerical evaluation results indicate that the proposed in a LIFO (Last In First Out) strategy combining the collective behaviors in the following aspects:(i) the evacuation of bottleneck are sensitive to evacuation strategy, e.g., passengers luggage distribution; (ii) evacuation time changes with the ferry passengers' evacuation strategy; (iii) passengers' satisfaction is enhanced since passenger waiting time decreasing and the good guidelines.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Green Multimodal Transport Path Optimization with the Participation of High-Speed Railway
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The development of green environmental protection concept puts forward higher requirements for transportation. The superior performance of high-speed railway makes it an inevitable trend to participate in the combined transportation of goods. In this paper, a multi-objective green multimodal transportation path optimization model is established by considering the restriction of node schedule and customer receiving time window. This model combines with three transportation modes of roads, waterway and high-speed railway. It aims to minimize carbon emissions and transportation costs while maximizing logistics service satisfaction. Non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm based on reference points (NSGA-III) is applied to solve the model. And the feasibility and effectiveness of the model and algorithm are verified by a numerical example, which provides a variety of transportation schemes to meet the differentiated needs of customers for multimodal transport operators.

articleTitle: Introducing a novel multi-objective optimization model for vehicle routing and relief supply distribution in post-disaster phase: combining fuzzy inference systems with NSGA-II and NRGA
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Each year, natural disasters cause many life losses as well as countless damages all over the world. So, implementing an efficient and effective relief supply distribution system to save human lives is of vital importance. To this end, we introduce a model to deal with two interdependent problems: vehicle routing problem (VRP) as well as relief distribution scheduling among demand points regarding three objective functions: First objective function is minimizing operational costs which include fixed and variable costs of using available heterogeneous fleet according to the designated route. Also, for more proper modeling of reality in the complex decision space of the response phase, two qualitative objective functions are introduced in this study: the importance of unmet demand and the importance of late-satisfied demand. For evaluating introduced qualitative indexes, we employ Fuzzy Inference Systems (FISs) to encapsulate decision makers' knowledge and human reasoning process. To solve the proposed model, FISs were embedded in Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and non-dominated ranked genetic algorithm (NRGA). Then algorithms were implemented on two categories of problems with small and large sizes and the performances of the algorithms were compared based on four criteria. The results of statistical tests showed that both algorithms have the same performance in small-size problems. However, NSGA-II outperforms NRGA in terms of runtime in large cases. As the objective functions are constructed based on FISs, the model can be adapted to various situations just by defining linguistic rules in the way that humans think and reason. Also, since the output of the algorithm is a trade-off among the objective functions in the form of Pareto optimal solutions, decision-makers can choose the best appropriate solution according to the circumstances.

articleTitle: Mode Design and Experiment of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Search and Rescue in Inland Waters
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The occurrence of accidents such as personnel falling into water requires higher rescue capability of search and rescue equipment. Traditional search and rescue methods based on ships and speedboats are difficult to find because their speed and visual field limit them. With the development of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) technology, UAV is gradually used in search and rescue work in inland rivers. This paper presents a method for U A V searching and rescuing on the inland rivers. First of all, Predicting the range of U A V search and rescue of inland river based on a prediction mode considering the influence of transverse and longitudinal slope of riverbank, wind, current, and wave on the drifting of the inland drowning person establishing a search and rescue range prediction model. Then design the U A V inland river and water search and rescue method according to the predicted range. According to the characteristics of the continuous expansion of the UAV search and rescue range, a mobile rectangular search method suitable for inland rivers is designed to determine the U A V’ s search distance. Finally, the proposed method is verified through experimental. By comparing the experimental results of UAV-based search and rescue and ship-based search and rescue, it is proved that the designed UAV -based search and rescue program can save time and improve efficiency.

articleTitle: Exploring the influencing factors on demand-responsive customized bus ridership using multi-source data
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Demand-responsive customized bus (DRCB) is a specific type of demand-responsive transit (DRT), which can flexibly customize services according to travel demand. However, few papers explored the influence factors on it. The purpose of this paper is to use the DRCB trip data from November 15 to December 15, 2020, in Xiongan New Area, China, to investigate the influence of built environment, weather, and time factors on DRCB ridership by using a negative binomial regression model. According to the spatiotemporal analysis, DRCB ridership is mainly concentrated in the peak hours of 07:00-09:00 and 17:00-20:00; the spatial distribution is primarily centered in areas such as government service center, railway station, and residential area. The model results show that scenic spot, governmental agency, morning peak period, and evening peak period are positively correlated with the DRCB ridership. Company, medical facility, visibility, rain, and weekend have a negative correlation with DRCB ridership. The results of this paper can provide insights for relevant companies to better understand the demand for DRCB and better plan the DRCB systems.

articleTitle: Research Progress of Ship Exhaust Gas Treatment Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: SOx, NOx and COx account for a high proportion of the exhaust gas of ships which take low quality heavy oil as fuel, resulting serious impact on the global environment. In this paper, three types of treatment technology of ship exhaust gas, i.e. pre-treatment technologies, in-cylinder control technologies and post treatment technologies, have been introduced. Various single post-treatment technologies for the control of ship exhaust gas pollutants emission, including marine scrubber, selective catalytic reduction (SCR) and carbon capture and storage (CCS) were reviewed. The advantages and limitations of various post-treatment technologies of Sox, NOX and COx were analyzed. In practice, single pollutant treatment technologies were not effective for ship exhaust emission reduction. The development of new desulfurizers, the optimization of integrated process flow, feasibility of the system operation, could be the future direction of ship exhaust post-treatment technology. There are two restrictions for the development of the ship exhaust treatment technology, which are the space limit and the cost requirements.

articleTitle: Classification, Design, and Challenges of Unmanned Ships in Marine Transportation
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Nowadays, there is a growing need for unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) for both military and civilian applications accompanied by a broader concept of smart or intelligent ships. In the past decade, various sizes and types of USVs have been developed to satisfy different marine purposes. However, most of the existing USVs are still in small sizes. In the future, large-scale unmanned ships for maritime transportation will be the final state of USVs. This paper focuses on the development phases, design components, and technology challenges of unmanned ships. After reviewing the state-of-the-art literature of research on USVs, the early stages of unmanned ships are categorized as conventional ships, enhanced ships, smart ships, remote-controlled ships, and autonomous ships. The design of unmanned ships is separated into ten components, which are the ground station, the ship station, the guidance, navigation, and control system, the communication system, the data collection system, the hull form, the maneuvering system, the propulsion system, the energy source, and test and measurements. Accordingly, the existing methods and challenges of the developments on unmanned ships are discussed.

articleTitle: An Information Flow Based Model for Navigation Risk Evolution in Fluctuating Backwater Zone of the Three Gorges Reservoir
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Due to the construction and operation of the Three Gorges Dam, the navigational conditions upstream of the Three Gorges Dam have changed considerably. The drastic change of water level upstream of the dam has caused great impact on the navigation safety of ships in this area. Ship accidents occur frequently, especially during the discharging period of the dam. A risk evolution model combining the HFACS model and information flow theory is proposed to analyze ship navigation safety in the fluctuating backwater zone. The proposed model introduces risk from the information flow perspective in three layers, which are macro-, meso-, and micro-levels. At each level, three characteristics of information flow, i.e., correctness, timeliness, and completeness, are considered as potential causal factors of navigation safety system risk. To demonstrate the feasibility of the model, the sinking of the cargo ship “EYiDuHuoShuangYa”, which caused serious consequences and attracted widespread social concern, was selected as a case study in this study. The results of the study can be used by maritime stakeholders to adopt countermeasures for ship navigation risk mitigation.

articleTitle: Research on PIN Photoelectric Non-contact Torque Measurement Device Based on Phase Difference
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: The quantitative accuracy of measuring shaft torque will directly determine the accuracy of shaft power measurement, and thus the reliability of ship condition monitoring. The research uses Solidworks mechanical design software to design corresponding installation accessories, which suppresses the torsional vibration effect caused by the rotation of the shaft and reduces the non-verticality effect caused by the installation of the photoelectric code disc. Use TINA circuit simulation software to analyze and verify the principle of the PIN photoelectric circuit, and develop the corresponding PIN photoelectric sensor, which speeds up the overall response time of the sensor. The processing of experimental data adopts the no-load average method to correct the torque measurement value to ensure This experiment was carried out on the shafting test platform. By drawing the torque and speed characteristic curve of the test system, the torque and speed characteristic error of the measuring device was analyzed, and the measurement accuracy of the photoelectric non-contact torque measuring device was verified. The experimental error is analyzed, and the reasons for the experimental error are discussed. The experimental results show that the method of combining simulation and experiment can improve the stability of the measuring device. This conclusion can provide a theoretical basis for the design and installation of photoelectric non-contact measurement devices based on phase difference and improve the measurement accuracy of such equipment.

articleTitle: Influence of different Machine learning algorithms on Prediction Model of Fuel Consumption of Inland Ships
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: An accurate prediction of ship fuel consumption is of great significance to the economy of ship operations. To study the influence of different machine learning algorithms on the prediction of ship fuel consumption, an inland river cruise ship has been considered as the research object. Based on the actual operation data obtained by the energy efficiency data acquisition system of the real ship, a prediction model of the ship's main engine fuel consumption was established using the Multi-Layer Perceptron Regression, Decision Tree Regression, Random Forest Regression, K-Nearest Neighbor, Extra Trees Regression and Support Vector Regression algorithms. Mean absolute error, mean square error, root mean square error, and coefficient of determination were used to evaluate the accuracy of the model, and the effect of different machine learning algorithms on the inland ship fuel consumption prediction model was investigated under different data volumes. The results show that the Extra Trees Regression and Random Forest Regression models perform best, and the amount of modelling data has a significant impact on the training time of the Random Forest Regression and Support Vector Regression models.

articleTitle: An AIS Data-Based Framework for Ship Allision Risk Assessment Near the Offshore Wind Farm
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: In order to investigate the allision risk of vessels near the Offshore Wind Farm (OWF) under the complicate surrounding environment, an AIS data-based allision risk framework is presented in this paper. The Bayesian learning approach is employed in this framework to learning the AIS database. The BN model of ship navigation behaviour near the OWF is then obtained. Meanwhile, the risk model that based on the output data from the BN under different combinations of navigation conditions is then used to assess the allision risk for new scenarios. A case study of an OWF is used to illustrate the application of the proposed model and the reliability of the new approach is tested. As a result, the proposed framework presents the evidence that impacts of OWF to vessels are diverse, which depend on ship categories, size and seasons. Fishing ships and OWF maintenance ships have smaller passing distance and that for oil and gas vessel is larger. Furthermore, ten cases have been ranked by using the proposed risk model. The developed risk allision framework from the empirical database provides a sufficient approach to evaluate the ship risk near the OWF, and further support the OWF safety management and ship navigating.

articleTitle: Using SHELL and Risk Matrix Method in Identifying the Hazards of General Aviation Flight Approach and Landing
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Safety is the sustainable development foundation of the general aviation, and the approach and landing phase is the most risky flight stage where aviation accidents frequently occur. In order to implement general aviation approach and landing safety management effectively from hazards identification and accidents prevention, Firstly, we sort out the logic and procedures of general aviation approach and landing flight manipulate based on the Hierarchical Task Analysis (HTA) method. Secondly, we use the SHELL model from Software(S), Hardware(H), Environment(E) and Liveware(L) four levels to identify the hazards comprehensively, then determine the occurrence severity and probability of hazards according to the risk matrix and the expert Delphi method, and determine the acceptability level of the hazards in the green, yellow and red different regions. Finally, safety engineering technology, regulation construction and education and training countermeasures are proposed, aiming at typical key hazards such as human factors and operating environment of approach and landing flight phase, which provides a reference for ensuring the flight safety of general aviation approach and landing.

articleTitle: Comparisons in Crash Rate and risky Behaviors between Novice Drivers and Experienced Drivers in China
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: Studies across many western countries have noted that driver experience is associated with crash risk. However, there are few studies conducted in China where driving patterns tend to be quite different. This paper uses crash fatality data from China for the year 2016 to examine the likelihood of crash involvement given driving experience. Driver behaviors contributing to crashes are investigated and compared among drivers' groups with more or less driving experience. The results reveal that the least experienced drivers have the highest crash rate, a crash rate that is approximately twice that of the crash rate of experienced drivers (> 3 years). Regarding fatal crashes, failing to yield and speeding are the most common risky behaviors by all drivers, no matter how experienced they are. The novice drivers' group has the largest crash number, but the proportions of risky behaviors for the groups with different driving experience are similar. A significantly large proportion of drivers with less than one year's driving experience are related to alcohol impairment and reversely driving. The conclusions may provide some implications for the related crash prevention and safety guidance for novice drivers.

articleTitle: Risk Management of Port Operations: a Systematic Literature Review and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2021 6th International Conference on Transportation Information and Safety (ICTIS)
abstract: With the continuous development of world economy, the trade and connection between countries are getting closer, in which ports are playing an increasingly important role. However, due to the inherent complexity of port operational environment, ports are exposed to various types of hazards and more likely to encounter risks with high frequency and serious consequences. Therefore, proper and effective risk management of ports is particularly essential and necessary. In this research, literature from three aspects including risk assessment of port operations and service, safety management of dangerous goods, and port supply chain risk management was collected and investigated, in order to put forward the future research direction related to the risk management of port operations.
